savùn.etymology: From Latin sāpōnem, accusative singular of sāpō, from Proto-Germanic *saipǭ.

savung.etymology: From Latin sāpōnem, accusative singular of sāpō, from Proto-Germanic *saipǭ.

belezza.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *bellitia, from Latin bellus. Compare Spanish belleza, Portuguese beleza, Occitan belesa, Catalan bellesa, Sicilian biddizza, Venetan bełézsa, Friulian bielece, Romansh baleztgia, Sardinian bellesa.

bellezia.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *bellitia, from Latin bellus. Compare Spanish belleza, Portuguese beleza, Occitan belesa, Catalan bellesa, Sicilian biddizza, Venetan bełézsa, Friulian bielece, Romansh baleztgia, Sardinian bellesa.

baleztgia.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *bellitia, from Latin bellus. Compare Spanish belleza, Portuguese beleza, Occitan belesa, Catalan bellesa, Sicilian biddizza, Venetan bełézsa, Friulian bielece, Romansh baleztgia, Sardinian bellesa.

battasenda.etymology: batta + senda, from batter (“beat”) and senda (“path”).

tscharvè.etymology: From Latin cerebellum, diminutive of cerebrum, from Proto-Italic *kerazrom, from a Proto-Indo-European form *ḱerh₂-s-ro, from the root *ḱerh₂- (“head”).

chastè.etymology: From Latin castellum, diminutive of castrum.

emblidar.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *oblītāre, a frequentative based on Latin oblīvīscor (via its past participle oblītus).

lubir.etymology: Maybe of West Germanic origin, compare German erlauben.

sumbriva.etymology: Probably from Latin umbra. Compare Spanish sombra.

retscha.etymology: Of Germanic origin, either akin to Old High German riga or Norwegian rekke.

glosses_en: a toilet with a built-in intimate washing facility

chatscha.etymology: Compare French chasse and Italian caccia.

girun.etymology: Deverbal from girar, due to their circling flight behavior.

glatscher.etymology: From Vulgar Latin *glaciārium. Equivalent to glatsch + -er. Compare Franco-Provençal gllaciér.

giumaint.etymology: Borrowed, probably from Italian giumento or perhaps directly from Latin iūmentum.

pavagl.etymology: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *papēlium, from Latin papȳrius.

gnieu.etymology: From Latin nīdus, from Proto-Italic *nizdos (“nest”), from Proto-Indo-European *nisdós (“nest”).

igniv.etymology: From Latin nīdus, from Proto-Italic *nizdos (“nest”), from Proto-Indo-European *nisdós (“nest”).
